question: Vitamin D from the skin or diet is metabolized primarily in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamine D3. What is the rate limiting enzyme in Vitamin D synthesis?

analysis: The synthesis of Vitamin D involves several steps, starting from the conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin to cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) upon exposure to UV light. This is then metabolized in the liver to 25-hydroxyvitamin D3. The rate-limiting step in the synthesis of the active form of Vitamin D is the conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3, which occurs in the kidney and is catalyzed by the enzyme 1-alpha-hydroxylase. Therefore, the rate-limiting enzyme in the synthesis of the active form of Vitamin D is 1-alpha-hydroxylase, which corresponds to the production of 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol.
